subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add a distinct soft-steer lifecycle that pauses or aborts active generation/tool work, injects user input, and resumes, or keep default steering as boundary-based queue delivery?
rationale: The remaining request affects shared runtime semantics, channel UX, Codex and native runtime contracts, and compatibility with existing steer, followup, collect, and interrupt modes.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with lifecycle, fallback, and backend-compatibility tests.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Treat current boundary-based steering as the supported default and limit follow-up work to messages reaching the existing queue policy.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Change default steer to stronger interruption semantics only after maintainer-approved upgrade proof across channels and runtimes.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with lifecycle, fallback, and backend-compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They owned the prior replacement attempt and merged adjacent session-state work that any soft-steer lifecycle must preserve.
